description: Plugin SDK - Create src/nexus/plugins/ package with plugin protocol, loader, registry, and hook system. Provides extensibility mechanism for NEXUS with lifecycle hooks for pre/post task execution, tool calls, and agent lifecycle events. Wire into main.py.
steps: Create src/nexus/plugins/__init__.py with package docstring and __all__ exports for all public classes

Create src/nexus/plugins/plugin_protocol.py with: (1) NexusPlugin Protocol class defining on_load() -> None, on_unload() -> None, get_tools() -> list[dict], get_hooks() -> dict[str, Callable] lifecycle methods, (2) PluginMetadata dataclass with name, version, author, description, dependencies fields, (3) PluginStatus enum (loaded, unloaded, error)

Create src/nexus/plugins/hook_system.py with: (1) HookPoint enum defining hook points: pre_task_execute, post_task_execute, pre_tool_call, post_tool_call, on_agent_create, on_agent_terminate, (2) HookContext dataclass providing context to hook handlers (agent_id, task_id, tool_name, timestamp, metadata dict), (3) HookManager class that registers handlers per hook point, executes them in order with error isolation (one handler failure does not block others), and supports priority ordering

Create src/nexus/plugins/plugin_loader.py with: (1) PluginLoader class that discovers plugins from a directory path (looks for Python files with a class implementing NexusPlugin protocol), (2) sandboxed_import function that imports a module in a restricted namespace (catches import errors, validates the module has the required protocol methods), (3) discover_plugins(directory: Path) -> list[PluginMetadata] function, (4) load_plugin(path: Path) -> NexusPlugin function

Create src/nexus/plugins/plugin_registry.py with: (1) PluginRegistry class managing loaded plugins as a dict[str, NexusPlugin], (2) register(plugin: NexusPlugin) method that calls on_load and stores the plugin, (3) unregister(name: str) method that calls on_unload and removes, (4) list_plugins() -> list[PluginMetadata], (5) get_plugin(name: str) -> NexusPlugin | None, (6) Integration with HookManager to auto-register plugin hooks on register

Wire into src/nexus/main.py: import PluginRegistry and HookManager, instantiate them in lifespan startup (after governance loading), store them in app.state for access by route handlers. Do NOT auto-load plugins from filesystem on startup (just initialize empty registry).

Create tests/test_plugin_sdk.py with comprehensive tests covering: NexusPlugin protocol conformance checks, HookManager registration/execution/error-isolation, PluginLoader discovery and sandboxed import (using temp directories with sample plugin files), PluginRegistry register/unregister/list/get lifecycle, hook execution order and priority
acceptance_criteria: src/nexus/plugins/ package exists with __init__.py, plugin_protocol.py, hook_system.py, plugin_loader.py, plugin_registry.py
NexusPlugin Protocol defines on_load, on_unload, get_tools, get_hooks methods
HookPoint enum has all 6 hook points: pre_task_execute, post_task_execute, pre_tool_call, post_tool_call, on_agent_create, on_agent_terminate
HookManager supports register, unregister, execute with error isolation
PluginLoader can discover and load plugins from a directory with sandboxed import
main.py instantiates PluginRegistry and HookManager in lifespan startup
tests/test_plugin_sdk.py has comprehensive tests for all components
All files pass Python AST parsing
verification: Run: python3 -c "import ast; import pathlib; [ast.parse(p.read_text()) for p in pathlib.Path('src/nexus/plugins').rglob('*.py')]"
Verify main.py contains PluginRegistry and HookManager initialization in lifespan
